known_gaps: All patient-facing clinical modules are draft and require clinician review.
All 53 drug choices and eight regimen choices now resolve a preparation guide, but only weekly paclitaxel, capecitabine monotherapy, and AC have exact treatment-specific preparation overlays.
The other five regimens and all standalone drugs use the clearly labelled general systemic-treatment preparation guide; Ariad does not infer exact preparation from drug classes or regimen components.
The 25 new symptom journeys are general systemic-treatment fallbacks. They do not establish that any exact drug or regimen caused or is associated with the selected symptom.
The three existing regimen-specific pathways remain the only exact treatment-and-symptom guidance relationships.
The eviQ hypersensitivity source is overdue for review and supports only infusion context and immediate reporting to the nurse; emergency signs are cross-checked against a current Canadian source.
The fictional demo clinic has unresolved fever and supportive-care policy bindings.
The exact AC schedule variant is unresolved; no nadir timing is included.
Catalogue-level treatment entries do not imply exact treatment guidance.
Thirty drugs have draft FDA evidence maps and patient presentations; all require clinician review.
Cyclophosphamide has a draft FDA label-category page without percentages, a usable denominator, or a claimed single-agent evidence population.
Doxorubicin has a draft FDA label-category page; the numerical AC table is retained only as excluded combination context and is not attributed to doxorubicin alone.
Epirubicin has a draft FDA label-category page; the numerical FEC and CEF tables are retained only as excluded combination context and are not attributed to epirubicin alone.
Pembrolizumab has a draft FDA single-agent label-category page across cancer types; KEYNOTE-522 combination values are excluded from individual-drug frequency mapping.
Twenty-three catalogue entries intentionally have no patient side-effect page.
Carboplatin uses the FDA 553-patient single-agent ovarian safety population; this does not claim an FDA breast-cancer indication or a TCH/TCHP regimen frequency.
Two broad catalogue sources are link-only and cannot enter a published release.

release_notes: Release 0.12.0 adds a source-linked general treatment-preparation guide, so all 61 treatment choices now resolve useful preparation information without implying exact treatment instructions.
Release 0.12.0 adds exact preparation overlays for weekly paclitaxel, capecitabine monotherapy, and AC, while keeping side-effect education available below preparation.
Release 0.12.0 adds explicit preparation ordering and exact-versus-general fallback labels; it does not add dose, schedule, food, medicine-change, fever-threshold, or local-policy instructions.
Release 0.12.0 keeps every new or revised patient module in draft with no recorded clinical approval.
Release 0.11.0 adds 25 unreviewed general symptom journeys, so all 28 symptom choices now have a complete six-section pathway in the preview.
Release 0.11.0 adds four patient-observable questions per new journey and keeps answers limited to a neutral fact summary and fixed-module ordering.
Release 0.11.0 adds 27 directly inspected source records from Ontario Health, BC Cancer, Canadian Cancer Society, Heart & Stroke, the Government of Canada, and eviQ.
Release 0.11.0 keeps all new objects in draft, labels the information as general, and does not add drug-specific symptom associations, diagnosis, grading, cause inference, or treatment-change advice.
Release 0.10.0 adds an unreviewed pembrolizumab page with the fourteen FDA single-agent common categories and principal serious immune-mediated warnings.
Release 0.10.0 excludes KEYNOTE-522 combination percentages and clearly identifies the common list as cross-cancer rather than breast-specific evidence.
Release 0.9.0 adds an unreviewed epirubicin page with fourteen FDA-supported common categories and four serious boxed-warning effects.
Release 0.9.0 excludes the FEC and CEF combination percentages from epirubicin's individual-drug frequency mapping and stores the denominator as unavailable.
Release 0.8.0 adds an unreviewed doxorubicin page with three FDA-supported common effects and four serious boxed-warning effects.
Release 0.8.0 excludes the AC combination percentages from doxorubicin's individual-drug frequency mapping and stores the denominator as unavailable.
Release 0.7.0 adds an unreviewed cyclophosphamide page with separate FDA-supported common and serious groups and no numerical frequency claims.
Release 0.7.0 stores cyclophosphamide denominator and event frequencies as unavailable and does not claim that its label-level safety evidence came from monotherapy.
Release 0.6.0 adds an unreviewed carboplatin patient page backed by the FDA 553-patient second-line single-agent ovarian safety population in Tables 7 and 8.
Release 0.6.0 keeps carboplatin's cross-indication population, denominator, exact percentages, dose context, and table mapping in private provenance rather than patient-display copy.
Release 0.5.0 adds unreviewed patient-only side-effect previews for the other 24 drugs with qualifying FDA breast-cancer single-agent frequency populations.
Release 0.5.0 records exact private FDA evidence for 25 drugs total and does not attribute combination-study rates to individual drugs.
Release 0.5.0 corrects the conventional paclitaxel record, which had pointed to a second albumin-bound paclitaxel label.
Release 0.4.0 adds one unreviewed patient-only docetaxel side-effect preview backed by a separately stored exact FDA evidence record.
Release 0.4.0 keeps FDA percentages, severity fields, laboratory thresholds, and dose context out of the patient-facing release payload.
Release 0.3.0 rebuilds drug search on exact current FDA breast-cancer treatment labels and canonical drug identities.
Release 0.3.0 keeps a canonical capecitabine drug result while offering two source-verified multi-drug regimens that contain it.
Release 0.3.0 adds separate TCH and TCHP regimen results with ordered component-drug destinations.
Release 0.2.0 separates structured clinic operations data from governed clinical-policy modules.
Release 0.1.1 corrects drug-level support labels so only complete regimen pathways display full guidance.
